question: A 55-year-old asthmatic patient goes to the ER with an exacerbation. One hour after the administration of supplemental oxygen and two nebulizations of salbutamol the patient does not improve. On examination, he breathed at 42 rpm with supraclavicular drainage and presented disseminated inspiratory and expiratory wheezing. The peak flow has dropped from 310 to 220 L / min. A gasometry extracted with oxygen at 28% shows a pO2 of 54 mmHg and a pCO2 of 35 mmHg. Which of the following attitudes seems LESS indicated?

options.opc: Nebulize ipratropium bromide together with salbutamol every 20 minutes.

enhanced_information: In this case of severe asthmatic exacerbation with hypoxemia and normal pCO2 levels, the least indicated action would be to increase oxygen flow. The patient already has a pO2 of 54 mmHg, indicating adequate oxygenation despite the exacerbation. Administering 80 mg of methylprednisolone iv, nebulizing ipratropium bromide with salbutamol every 20 minutes, administering intravenous magnesium, and starting non-invasive mechanical ventilation are all appropriate interventions based on consensus guidelines for managing severe asthma exacerbations.
analysis: In a severe asthmatic exacerbation with hypoxemia and normal pCO2 levels, increasing oxygen flow is not the recommended action as the patient already has adequate oxygenation. Administering 80 mg of methylprednisolone iv, nebulizing ipratropium bromide with salbutamol every 20 minutes, administering intravenous magnesium, and starting non-invasive mechanical ventilation are appropriate interventions. Therefore, the least indicated action is to increase oxygen flow.
